original_question: Can one characterize the groups pi_1^(r)(X) geometrically, without referring to stratified vector bundles; equivalently, can one describe which Galois coverings of X have the property that the natural surjection pi_1(X) -> G factors through pi_1^(r)(X)?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Question 4.5 of Carlo Gasbarri’s note “Flat connections and representations of the fundamental group in characteristic p > 0,” together with the immediately following sentence explaining the question in terms of Galois coverings whose quotient map π_1(X) → G factors through π_1^{(r)}(X). ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_2005__113__129_0.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target very closely: it asks for a geometric characterization of the groups π_1^{(r)}(X), explicitly avoids referring to stratified vector bundles, and includes the paper’s own gloss via factorization of the surjection π_1(X) → G attached to a Galois covering. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_2005__113__129_0.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient setting is omitted: k is the algebraic closure of a finite field, X is a connected smooth projective curve over k, and F : X → X is the absolute Frobenius. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_2005__113__129_0.pdf))
The parameter r must be fixed and positive; the paper says “for every positive integer r.” ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_2005__113__129_0.pdf))

The notation π_1^{(r)}(X) is not defined in the draft. In the paper it is the Tannaka group attached to the Tannakian category SS(X)_r. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_2005__113__129_0.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, one must define SS(X)_r: its objects are sequences {E_n, σ_n} where E_n is a vector bundle on X, σ_n : F^*(E_n) ≅ E_{n-1}, and Card({(E_n, σ_n)}) ≤ r. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_2005__113__129_0.pdf))

For stand-alone precision, the relevant coverings should be described as finite étale Galois coverings Y → X, since the paper is using the algebraic fundamental group π_1(X). This is implicit in the surrounding representation-theoretic and Galois-covering language. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_2005__113__129_0.pdf))

The phrase “geometrically” should not be left broad: in the paper it is immediately narrowed to the problem of characterizing exactly those Galois coverings Y → X for which π_1(X) → Gal(Y/X) factors through π_1^{(r)}(X). ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_2005__113__129_0.pdf))
refined_question: Fix a positive integer r. Let k be the algebraic closure of a finite field, let X be a connected smooth projective curve over k, and let π_1^{(r)}(X) denote the Tannaka group of the Tannakian subcategory SS(X)_r whose objects are sequences {E_n, σ_n} with E_n a vector bundle on X, σ_n : F^*(E_n) ≅ E_{n-1}, and Card({(E_n, σ_n)}) ≤ r. Can one characterize π_1^{(r)}(X) geometrically, without mentioning stratified vector bundles; that is, can one characterize the finite étale Galois coverings Y → X whose associated quotient map π_1(X) → Gal(Y/X) factors through π_1^{(r)}(X)? ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_2005__113__129_0.pdf))
justification: The draft does not point to the earlier Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 material elsewhere in the proceedings; it clearly matches Gasbarri’s separate note in Section 4. The note first fixes the setting k, X, and F, recalls the equivalence between stratified bundles and sequences {E_n, σ_n}, then defines the subcategories SS(X)_r and the associated Tannakian groups π_1^{(r)}(X). Immediately afterward, Question 4.5 asks for a geometric characterization of the π_1^{(r)}(X)’s, and the next sentence explains exactly that this means characterizing the Galois coverings whose quotient π_1(X) → G factors through π_1^{(r)}(X). Your draft is therefore essentially on target, but it needs the field/curve hypotheses, the fixed integer r, and the definition of π_1^{(r)}(X) to be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_2005__113__129_0.pdf))
